tip: Brille is singular in German, even though English 'glasses' is plural: eine neue Brille = one pair of glasses.
After ein (neuter), the adjective takes -es: ein interessantes Buch. The -es carries the neuter marker the article leaves off.
leihen marks the person receiving in the dative: seinem Mitbewohner = to his roommate.
kennenlernen is separable, so 'zu' goes inside it: kennenzulernen, not 'zu kennenlernen'.
To negate a noun, use kein, which declines like ein: keinen Parkplatz = not any parking space (masc. accusative).
musst nicht means 'don't have to', not 'must not'. For a ban you would say darfst nicht.
kein ... mehr means 'not any more': keine Lust mehr = doesn't feel like it anymore.
vertrauen takes a dative object, not accusative: sie vertraut dem Bergführer = she trusts the guide.
Verbs ending in -ieren form the participle without ge-: funktioniert, not 'gefunktioniert'.
After die (singular feminine), the adjective takes -e: die neue Lehrerin.
Inseparable prefixes like ver- drop the ge- in the participle: verdoppelt, not 'geverdoppelt'.
an + dem contracts to am for days and weekends: Am Wochenende = on the weekend.
Add -erweise to an adjective to make a sentence adverb: Bedauerlicherweise = regrettably.
German has no verb 'to like doing'; add gern to a verb instead. nicht gern = dislikes doing it.
Der Nachbar is a weak noun, so it adds -n outside the nominative: dem Nachbarn.
der Verstorbene is an adjective used as a noun, so it keeps adjective endings: dem Verstorbenen.
Amount plus contents stand side by side with no word for 'of': eine Flasche Wein = a bottle of wine.
in shows movement here, so it takes the accusative: in ein Café. For a fixed location it would take the dative.
A stretch of time in the accusative needs no preposition: jeden Tag = every day.
schlafen changes its a to ä in the er/sie/es form: sie schläft = she sleeps.
Dative feminine ends in -er: meiner Mutter = to my mother, the person receiving what is shown.
vorbereiten is separable, so the prefix vor jumps to the end: bereite ich den Nachtisch vor.
Genitive 'of the' uses des for masc/neuter and adds -s to the noun: des Herbstlaubs = of the autumn foliage.
sollen means 'be supposed to' and pushes the main verb to the end as an infinitive: soll ... kontrollieren.
